title: The DVFS loop and its leakage · ET-SoC-1
description: David Kanter described how a mature chip regulates its own power: an activity-based estimator inside a DVFS loop, and cache arrays behind leakage-suppression transistors. Checked against the ET-SoC-1's firmware source, its open RTL and, on 26 September, three cards: the loop reads a power meter rather than estimating power, compares the mean of 34 shire sensors (never the hottest) and, with no dead band, hunts at its 65 °C threshold on aifoundry2, where a development night (28 September, not yet validated) saw the step follow that mean and perimeter placement hold 800 MHz longer; the open RTL has per-minion sleep controls, tied off, and no card shows array power gating; on aifoundry2 at 80 °C leakage is 55–80% of an idle card, against his 5–30%, while more than 30% of a busy one is not established; and a boot service's TDP of 0 W pins aifoundry3 at 600 MHz.
